questions.q: What is the key difference between static (inline) SOQL and dynamic SOQL?
options: Dynamic SOQL can only be used in Batch Apex
Dynamic SOQL cannot use WHERE clauses
Static SOQL always runs faster than dynamic SOQL
Dynamic SOQL builds the query text itself as a string at runtime; static SOQL has its query shape fixed at compile time
questions.explain: Static SOQL's query shape is fixed at compile time (even though bind variable values can vary); dynamic SOQL constructs the query text itself as a runtime string.

options: Always a specific typed list like List<Account>
A generic SObject or List<SObject>, since Apex doesn't know the concrete type at compile time
An AggregateResult
A QueryLocator
questions.explain: Because the object being queried is only known at runtime, Database.query returns the generic SObject/List<SObject> type.

questions.q: What is Database.getQueryLocator specifically meant for?
options: Running a query without any governor limits
Pulling records directly into memory the same way Database.query does
Batch Apex or Visualforce controllers processing a potentially huge result set in manageable chunks
Converting a SOQL query into a SOSL search
questions.explain: A QueryLocator is designed for chunked processing of large result sets in Batch Apex or Visualforce, not for direct in-memory retrieval.

options: Just the count of records the query would match, without fetching them
The full list of matching records
A boolean indicating whether any records matched
The query's estimated execution cost from the Query Plan tool
questions.explain: countQuery returns only the matching record count, avoiding the cost of actually retrieving the records themselves.

questions.q: In user mode (AccessLevel.USER_MODE), what is enforced on a dynamic query that may NOT be enforced in system mode?
options: Whether the query is static or dynamic
Governor limits on the number of SOQL queries per transaction
The maximum OFFSET value
The running user's object permissions, field-level security, and sharing rules
questions.explain: User mode applies the running user's actual object/field permissions and sharing rules, the same as a query run through the UI; system mode bypasses these.
